text: Suitor offers can already be reproduced from the bench save, and the saved scroll reopens the old wife offer every time it loads. The gap is a wife offer on a fresh turn, which is what would prove the marrying code and the new wording. The saved scroll can't do that, because that offer has already fired, so for now it's proven only when the game happens to roll one. The engine exposes marriage age limits and a marryWife call, but I haven't looked at them yet.

The spy report close is merged and the unit tests pass. Its first live run, when one of your spies succeeds, hasn't happened yet, and the one-shot check for it is still running. The roll is 25% per turn, so it could take a while. The campaign watch is on and I'll report when it fires. Next is designing the live test for the rest of the suite.

The bot's clock handling is live and the arena matches look healthy. Claim-victory has not fired in anger yet. It needs an opponent to actually abandon a game, which happens on its own every so often, so the code path stays unexercised against the live server until one does. Everything else from today's list is merged and running.

The publish script is merged and the first run worked end to end, with the page up at the expected address. One gap remains: anything in that script that only runs on a second publish is untested until a second publish happens, so the update path and the old-version cleanup haven't been run by anything yet. I'll keep an eye on it next time.

I ran the hook command by hand: it printed 35 lines with no error, and the test suite passes with 784 tests. It hasn't fired for real yet, because that only happens on an actual compaction, and this session may never reach one. The next long session should show whether the handoff text really lands in front of the model afterwards.

The method is frozen today and judged only on draws that haven't happened yet. It's slow but fully honest, because a pre-registered forward test means nobody can tune it after seeing results. Forcing or back-filling a result would ruin the experiment, so the wait is the method. The first scored draw is on the calendar, and the status file shows counts only.

The judge is built and the pre-registration is written. One fork for you to decide: whether it casts its chart at the draw studio, which can be checked against past draws, or at your location when you ask, which is forward only. Scoring waits on future draws in both cases, as the protocol requires, so there's nothing to speed up there.

The gate now refuses to publish the lid until its dimensions are measured. It needs five caliper readings from the printed coupon, which only you can take, since the whole point is checking the real part against the model. Once you send them, I'll mark all five as measured, rebuild and confirm the gate shows the lid as publishable. Then the next step is printing the fit coupon.

The bench reproduced it. That's the papal crash we thought was fixed, and the bench caught it in 2 minutes instead of waiting for it to happen in a live campaign. The log shows the death at 05:29:28, the election scroll a second later, and the crash on the next click. The fix is on a branch with a failing test that now passes.

Merged as PR 212 and main matches the remote. The full suite passes with 2,684 tests and 4 skipped, and the install gate passed in 70 seconds on the final commit. I reran the bench after the merge and all 12 saves are green. There's nothing left on this item, and the next one on the roadmap is the retrieval recall bench.

The release trigger is merged, and the tests cover the version comparison with fake data. Tomorrow's 03:00 log should show the package upgraded to the new version, which brings in the fix. That's the one open item in my todo. The real job hasn't run with this change yet, so the upgrade step itself hasn't been seen working from end to end.

The garrison code and the mercenary order are merged, and the fake-game tests pass. They also flag when money is sitting unspent while a town is under threat. The new code hasn't run against the real game yet: the background check is still waiting for the first live siege or mercenary hire, so that path stays unproven until one comes up in the campaign.

The plan is written and shows six new helpers, two automations and one dashboard page, and nothing else in the house changes. I ran it in check mode against a copy of the config and it applied cleanly there. Say go and I'll apply it to the real system. It takes a backup first, then I'll run the plan again to confirm the house matches.

The address can't be added back yet. The mail provider holds a removed address for a while before it can be reused, and their support page says this can take a day or so. Nothing on our side is wrong, and the forwarding rule is saved and ready. It should start working once their system releases the address, and there's no way to hurry that up from here.

The bot is running at the new level and the config is committed. The startup line shows the right level, and the first game finished normally. After about ten rated games its rating will show whether this level plays at the target strength, and then we move it up or down one. That takes real games against real opponents, so it will take a day or two.

The new orders prompt is live in this run. The thing to watch is whether the refusal rate, 23% so far against 57% in the last run, and the empty-garrison problem keep improving over the next ten turns or so. It's too early to call from three turns. I'll look at the numbers when the watch next wakes me, and report them with the run summary.

The config change and the migration are written and tested on a copy. Recreating the container would end the game that's on right now, so I'm holding the recreate until that game finishes, and the restart will pick up the new settings when it runs. Once it has, I'll check that the startup line shows the new value and that the player count is unchanged.

The install finished and transcription works, with the model loaded in about 3.6 GB. When idle it adds no GPU load, and it only computes while transcribing. One thing to know for later: a future compiler upgrade could break this build, since the toolkit is picky about compiler versions. If that ever happens, the fix is one extra flag in the build step.

The live worktree is set up, and the dry run passed. Next I'll enable the timer in dry-run mode so that it starts collecting the six dry slots the protocol requires before anything counts. The slots run at 10:35 and 20:35, so six take three days, and that spacing is part of the pre-registered design. The status command shows how many are done.

I found two config files with the same setting and different values, and the running service reads the second. The first looks like a leftover from the old install. Nothing depends on it that I can find, and removing it would make the setup simpler, but it's your machine and it holds a credential, so I've left it in place and listed it in the handoff.
